home.title: Code Owl
home.subtitle: Generate tiered Parsons puzzles. Faster differentiation for computer science education.
home.generating: Generating, this may take a moment...
home.tip1: You can provide a problem statement, a code snippet, programming concepts and/or a language — the system fills in missing inputs.
home.tip2: Without a code snippet, the programming language must be specified so the model uses the correct syntax.
home.tip3: Use clear concepts (e.g. Loop, Condition, Collections) for more precise and pedagogically meaningful tasks.
home.tip4: Keep problem statements short, clear and behavior-focused — avoid variable or method names.
home.tip5: Try the demo example to see the expected format.
home.tip6: Inputs can be in German or English — better results with English.
home.tip7: For more information use the help page (bottom left).
home.contextModeEnabled: Context mode — longer code with scaffolding (Beta)
home.blacklistHint: Comma-separated. These constructs will NOT appear in generated code.
home.whitelistHint: Comma-separated. If set, ONLY these constructs may appear.
home.additionalContextPlaceholder: e.g. Use German variable names, Focus on string manipulation
home.additionalContextHint: Free-text instructions injected into the generation prompt.
home.tierCountHint: 5-Tier mode uses a dedicated pedagogical progression prompt.

manual.title: Manual Task Creator
manual.subtitle: Create Parsons puzzle tasks from your own code — without AI generation.
manual.problemPlaceholder: Describe the task, e.g.: 'Arrange the code blocks to create a function that reverses a string.'
manual.problemHelper: Supports Markdown. Be specific about what the code should do.
manual.previewEmpty: Type code on the left to see a live preview of the Parsons blocks.
manual.tipLines: Each non-empty line becomes a draggable block.
manual.tipIndent: Indentation is preserved — students must indent blocks correctly.
manual.tipLength: Keep solutions under ~15 lines for the best puzzle experience.
manual.tipDifficulty: Tier 1 should be the easiest, Tier 3 the hardest.
manual.tipVariation: You can use different code per tier or the same code with different problem statements.
manual.conceptRequired: At least one concept is required.
